title: No narrow read: task view --max-notes rejects 0, and task list has no projection at all
description:
Reported by lore-cli via opum-agent 2026-09-15 21:10Z, ranked their second-largest context consumer after a harness interaction they cannot control. Confirmed NOT a usage mistake -- I checked for an existing narrow read before accepting the report, and the interesting part is what I found.

MEASURED HERE against QCLI-307, a 7-note record, quest 0.7.1:

  quest task view QCLI-307 --plain                22582 bytes
  quest task view QCLI-307 --json                 22725 bytes
  quest task view QCLI-307 --max-notes 1 --plain   7129 bytes   <- the current floor
  quest task view QCLI-307 --max-notes 0           REJECTED: "--max-notes must be a positive integer"
  quest task list --limit 1 --plain                6062 bytes
  quest task list --limit 3 --plain               27205 bytes
  quest task list --max-notes 1                   REJECTED: "Unrecognized flag --max-notes"

THE SHARP PART: `task view` ALREADY HAS the flag that would express a zero-note projection, and it rejects exactly the value that solves the problem. `--max-notes 0` is the natural spelling, a caller will try it first, and it errors. The floor a caller can currently reach is --max-notes 1 at 7129 bytes, which still pays for one full note body. So half this ask is a one-line change to a validator, not a new feature.

`task list` is the worse half and has no projection at all: it prints full records including every note, so 27 KB answered a question about three ids. The reporter sharpest case is that `quest task list --status "In Progress"` -- which this fleet asks every session to run before reporting clear, a duty designed to be cheap -- dumps whole records to answer "which id".

WHY IT IS MORE THAN CONVENIENCE: quest is read by agent sessions whose context is a hard budget, and the fleet was recycling three over-budget sessions simultaneously the night this was reported. The tax is paid most heavily by the tasks with the richest notes, which are exactly the tasks under active work. Note also that I ran `quest task list --status "In Progress"` many times this session and never saw the cost, because nothing was In Progress and it printed "(empty)" -- the duty is cheap precisely when there is nothing to report and expensive exactly when there is.

TWO INDEPENDENT CONSUMERS now ask for read shaping: lore-cli here, and mbpm2 externally (field selection, note cursors, individual-note reads, zero-note projections -- recorded as context on QCLI-310). That is corroboration from different directions rather than one team preference.

ACCEPTANCE EXAMPLE the reporter gave, shape deliberately left open:
  quest task list --status "In Progress" --oneline
  LCLI-510  In Progress  Shipped README advertises the previous version

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest task view <id> --max-notes 0 is accepted and returns the record with no note bodies, rather than being rejected as not a positive integer
quest task list gains a projection that answers id/status/title without note bodies, measured as a byte reduction against the 27205-byte three-task baseline recorded in the description
The narrow read is what the fleet reporting duty can use: quest task list --status In Progress returns ids and titles without dumping records
Both --plain and --json honour the projection, since the agent callers this is for read --json and the 22725-byte --json figure is the one that actually bites them
mbpm2 and lore-cli are told the outcome, since they are the two independent consumers whose reports established the need

implementationNotes: Cross-referenced during a fleet-wide dedupe pass, 2026-09-17: related to but not a duplicate of QCLI-291 (task views deferred DEC-3 --fields projection scope). That task is about task views general field projection; this one is about task views --max-notes 0 edge case plus task list having no projection mechanism at all -- a different command surface and a narrower, already-concretely-scoped ask backed by two named consumers (mbpm2, lore-cli). Left as two independent tasks rather than merged or parented, since collapsing them would lose this tasks specific, actionable acceptance criteria.
